journey.title: Take a scenario from source to an installable app
journey.purpose: The primary loop, initiated from a Linux host that cannot build for iOS at all. An owner picks a scenario, generates an iOS app, watches it build and validate on a remote macOS node, and learns exactly what remains before a person can install it. The journey must complete with no Apple Developer Program enrollment, ending honestly at a named blocker.

steps.intent: Start from a host with no reachable macOS node and distinguish the permanently unsupported rows from the ones merely waiting on a node.
Confirm that the local native target explains its terminal state and offers nothing to click.
With a macOS node online, see which node will execute the work and start a validation run.
Read the conformance chapters, confirm the semantic strategy produced them, and confirm the app satisfies the iOS platform contract.
Learn that the artifact is proven but not shippable, see the first concrete action, and learn that a physical-device path exists that needs no enrollment.

claims.statement: The journey is walkable from a Linux host, and the difference between 'this host never can' and 'no node is available' is legible at the first step.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-003. This is the ramp's defining condition. If the two states read the same, the operator cannot tell a missing machine from a category error.

claims.statement: The full journey completes with no Apple Developer Program enrollment, ending at a named blocking rung rather than an error.
claims.rationale: S2I-P0-009. An owner must be able to prove their app works before spending $99. A flow that dead-ends on missing enrollment conflates validation with release.

claims.statement: At every step where work executes remotely, the executing node is named.
claims.rationale: Remote execution is the normal path here. Hiding it makes a remote failure indistinguishable from a local one.

claims.statement: A fully passing matrix never presents itself as ready to ship while release readiness rungs are unsatisfied.
claims.rationale: The two axes are independent. Conflating them is how an owner discovers at upload time that they cannot publish.
